1.9.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, Pasal 1 angka (10) defines “Kekerasan terhadap Perempuan” to include “eksploitasi ekonomi, sosial” (economic and social exploitation), and Pasal 1 angka (13) defines “Kekerasan Seksual” broadly as acts targeting a person’s body/sexuality causing harm. While the regulation does not explicitly use the term “perbudakan seksual” (sexual slavery), it does explicitly cover “eksploitasi” as part of violence against women/children. The retrieved English candidates included this definition (candidate [1.9-6] contains “economic exploitation, social”), so the judge had relevant information but applied an overly narrow standard by requiring explicit mention of sexual exploitation/sexual slavery and therefore answered No.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION
OF WEST SERAM REGENCY
NUMBER 08 OF 2019
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION
FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has the obligation to provide Protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Women and Children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience Violence and therefore need to receive Protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any unlawful act, with or without using instruments/means, against the physical and psychological integrity that causes danger to life or the body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Furthermore, Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services and therefore comprehensive implementation of Protection for Women and Children is required.

In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in West Seram Regency (SBB) so as to avoid Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children particularly with regard to institutional matters, forms and mechanisms of prevention, prevention of acts of Violence, accompaniment mechanisms, services for Victims of acts of Violence and empowerment of Victims of acts of Violence.

4.2.rationale: The original Indonesian text does include prevention-oriented education/socialization content. Pasal 8 huruf a states “kegiatan sosialisasi peraturan perundang-undangan kepada masyarakat yang berkaitan dengan Perlindungan hak Perempuan dan Anak” (outreach/socialization of laws to the community related to protection of women’s and children’s rights). Pasal 23 ayat (2) huruf f also states “melakukan sosialisasi hak perempuan dan anak secara mandiri” (conduct independent socialization of women’s and children’s rights). These are clearly educational/socialization activities aimed at primary prevention. The judge’s cited snippet matches Pasal 23(2)(f) and is consistent with the Indonesian. Therefore the predicted Yes is supported, and the golden label “No” appears incorrect.

6.5.evaluator_rationale: People with disabilities are mentioned as part of the definition of victims/vulnerable groups, but there are no special protection measures or disability-specific services described for women with disabilities or persons with disabilities.

The retrieved candidates shown to the judge included this exact point (candidate [6.5-6] includes “vulnerable groups, such as persons with disabilities”). The judge nonetheless answered No because it looked for disability-specific services/measures; however, the indicator is “People with disability” and the policy does address it by explicitly naming disability as a vulnerable group within the definition of victims. So the error is the judge being too strict, not missing evidence.

The official elucidation (Penjelasan) for Pasal 25 huruf b explicitly clarifies that “sumber lain yang sah” includes “bantuan dana dari Pemerintah Pusat” (funding assistance from the Central/National Government), as well as Province and NGOs. This directly supports a Yes for “National government budget” as an allowed funding source. (29) Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as LPPA, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional government to provide services to Women and Child victims of violence comprehensively and with quality including Information services related to victims' rights, Complaint handling services for victims of violence against women and children, Health services for women and child victims of violence, Psychosocial services for women and child victims of violence, legal accompaniment services and repatriation and Social Reintegration services as well as safe house services through a referral mechanism. (30) Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to implement Prevention and Protection activities for Women and Child Victims of acts of Violence. (31) Safe House is temporary housing provided to give Protection to Victims in accordance with predetermined standards. (32) Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. (33) Woman is an adult human of female gender and a person recognized by law as a Woman. (34) Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. (35) Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman and/or Child. (36) Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. (37) The Implementation of Protection for Women and Children is carried out based on the principles of:
 a. respect for human rights; b. non-discrimination; c. justice and gender equality; d. the best interests of the Child; e. respect for the opinions of Women and Children; and
 f. justice and protection for women and child Victims of Violence. g. The right of children to life, survival, and development. (38) The Implementation of Protection for Women and Children aims to:
 a. provide Services and Protection to Women and child victims of violence from gender-based violence and the best interests of children that occur in the home and community (public); b. prevent all forms of Violence against Women and Children; and
 c. empower Women and Child Victims of Violence. (39) The scope of Protection for Women and Children includes:
 a. institutions; b. forms and handling mechanisms; c. prevention of acts of violence against women and children; d. accompaniment mechanisms; e. services for Victims of acts of Violence; f. Recovery of victims of acts of violence; and
 g. empowerment of Victims and their families.

 b. education and training for Women Victims of Violence;
 c. educational assistance for Women and Child Victims of Violence who have been withdrawn from education; and
 d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of Women Victims of Violence.
(3) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are implemented in the form of an agreement.
